note: Adapted from the species description of Sjöstedt (1900), originally in German; the original deals mainly with the soldier, the alate is recorded as unknown and one larva is also described; ratios of mandible to head width and measurements such as head length and width are incomplete in the OCR and are not transcribed; figure numbers and locality records are omitted.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule cylindrical, flattened dorsoventrally, rectangular, angles rounded, anterior margin almost straight, twice as long as wide, chestnut brown, slightly paler posteriorly; frons inclined forward, broadly concave; vertex slightly flattened along the midline; mandibles slightly shorter than head width, stout to the base, shiny black, only very weakly curved upward in profile, left mandible with three distinct, rather large, sharp teeth, two of them near the apex, right mandible with two very large teeth in the basal half; labrum ligulate, flattened anteriorly, bearing a tuft of fine hairs, slightly longer than wide; antennae 17-segmented, slender, slightly longer than half the head, base surrounded by a prominent collar, almost imperceptibly tapering outwards; first segment distinctly larger than the third, third larger than the following segments; eye a very small, oval but distinct pale spot behind the antennal fossa; pronotum large, slightly wider than the head, not transversely rectangular but more nearly semicircular; anterior angles rounded and rectangular, lateral angles rounded and slightly obtuse; lateral margins almost straight; posterior margin a very weak arc, slightly concave at midlength; anterior margin distinct, broadly concave; meso- and metanotum slightly narrower than the pronotum and equal in width to each other, rectangular, posterior angles weakly produced, sometimes a little more strongly so; legs short and stout, with small appendicular lobes between the claws; whole body including the legs yellowish white, thoracic sclerites tinged brown, shining, covered with very fine short hairs.

sections.label: Nymph
sections.text: One further larva, about 8 mm long, with the posterior angles of the mesonotum and especially of the metanotum slightly produced; thoracic sclerites as in the soldier, with a fine line running through the middle.
